title: SQL Injection in User Search Functionality
description: The user search endpoint was vulnerable to SQL injection attacks due to string concatenation in database queries.
root_cause: Direct string concatenation in LINQ query construction instead of using parameterized queries.
resolution: Replaced all string concatenation with Entity Framework parameterized queries. Implemented input validation and sanitization.
code_changes: Implemented SQL injection detection in integration tests
lessons_learned: Always use parameterized queries or ORM methods
Implement automated security testing in CI/CD pipeline
Regular security code reviews are essential
prevention_measures: Added static analysis rules to detect string concatenation in queries
Created coding standard for database access patterns

title: N+1 Query Problem in User Profile Page
description: User profile page was experiencing severe performance issues due to N+1 query pattern when loading user data with related entities.
root_cause: Entity Framework lazy loading causing separate database queries for each related entity (orders, addresses, preferences).
resolution: Implemented eager loading with Include() statements and created optimized projection queries for the profile view.
code_changes: Added .Include(u => u.Orders).Include(u => u.Addresses) to user queries
Created ProfileDto with projection query to select only needed fields
Implemented caching for frequently accessed profile data
lessons_learned: Always profile database queries during development
Use Entity Framework Include() for related data
Consider projection queries for view-specific data
prevention_measures: Added performance tests to CI/CD pipeline
Implemented database query logging in development
Created performance review checklist for data access code

title: Memory Leak in File Processing Service
description: Application was experiencing gradual memory increase and eventual OutOfMemoryException during large file processing operations.
root_cause: Large file streams and image objects were not being properly disposed, accumulating in memory and preventing garbage collection.
resolution: Implemented proper disposal patterns using 'using' statements and IDisposable for all resource-heavy operations.
code_changes: Wrapped all Stream operations in using statements
Implemented IDisposable in FileProcessor and ImageResizer classes
Added explicit GC.Collect() calls after processing large batches
Replaced large object caching with streaming approach
lessons_learned: Always implement IDisposable for classes that handle unmanaged resources
Use using statements consistently for Stream and graphics objects
Monitor memory usage during development and testing
prevention_measures: Added memory usage monitoring to application metrics
Implemented automated memory leak detection tests
Created guidelines for handling large files and unmanaged resources

title: Authentication Timing Attack Vulnerability
description: Login endpoint was vulnerable to timing attacks allowing attackers to enumerate valid usernames based on response time differences.
root_cause: Different code paths for valid vs invalid usernames resulted in measurable timing differences (valid users: ~200ms, invalid users: ~50ms).
resolution: Implemented constant-time authentication by always performing password hash verification regardless of username validity.
code_changes: Modified authentication to always compute password hash even for invalid users
Added consistent delay mechanism for all authentication responses
Implemented rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks
lessons_learned: Authentication operations must have consistent timing
Consider timing attacks during security design
Implement proper rate limiting for authentication endpoints
prevention_measures: Added timing analysis to security testing suite
Implemented monitoring for authentication timing patterns
